thought.text: All validation checks passed. Here is my report.

reasoning_content:
Everything verified. Let me note: guide says `bin/dev` uses `forego`. The summary says foreman was installed instead because forego had no binary. bin/dev itself wasn't modified (it still calls forego). But that's a minor deviation from the guide's documented command; the app is operational via foreman. The core requirement — running Zammad at localhost:3000 with login — is met.

Let me check whether forego is installed. Actually this is a nuance. The guide documents `bin/dev`. The installer used `foreman start -f Procfile.dev`. Both achieve the same. Not a failure since the software is operational.

Let me compile the report as success.

action.message: Validation complete. Zammad is installed correctly and is fully operational per the supplied guide (Manual Setup method).

I confirmed the toolchain matches declared requirements (Ruby 3.4.9 per .ruby-version, Node v24.21.0 / pnpm 11.25.0 per package.json engines), and that the three backing services required by Zammad are running: PostgreSQL 14 (zammad_development DB with 131 tables and seeded users), Redis (PONG), and Elasticsearch 8.15.5 (>= 8.15 requirement) with Zammad's per-model indices created. I verified actual application behavior rather than file existence: the root page returns HTTP 200 with the Zammad title, static assets (application.js/css) return 200 indicating asset compilation succeeded, and a full authenticated signin using the guide's documented credentials (admin@example.com / test) returns HTTP 201 and a valid session (confirming the CSRF+fingerprint API flow and that seeded admin credentials work). All five Procfile.dev services (puma web:3000, vite, websocket-server:6042, background-worker, dartsass:watch) are listening/running, and the websocket server completes a real HTTP 101 upgrade handshake. Config (config/database.yml, es_url setting) and DB/job state were verified via psql and `rails runner`.\n\nLimitations/notes: The guide's recommended devcontainer path was not used (VS Code \\\"Reopen in Container\\\" unavailable headless); the installer used the documented Manual Setup path, so devcontainer-only files are not required and their absence is not a failure. The summary notes foreman was substituted for forego (bin/dev still invokes forego), but startup via `foreman start -f Procfile.dev` launches the same Procfile.dev process set and the application is fully operational, so this does not affect the outcome. No files were modified and no setup/migrations were performed during validation."}
